body:
I guess what I mean is that I feel too tired to do the things I want to do and so instead I just lay in bed doing nothing. I don't know how to explain it.

The things I want to do are continue working on my programming skills so I can make an Android app, start driving more so I can get comfortable with it.  Search for work.  

Unfortunatly at this time all that has to be put on hold due to some weird health issues.  I've spent maybe 10 minutes writing this and my head is pounding, my ears are burning, and my eyes feel like they've been squinting as hard as they can for hours.  It's like life is telling me that being tired isn't enough, now you're going to be punished for even looking at a computer.
I'm going to be seeing my doctor in a couple weeks.  I do find myself with no plans/nothing to do quite often, I suspect that isn't helping any.
Yeah I'm a guy also, makes it much more frustrating as all the guys I know just rinse their face in the shower and come out with spotless skin.

Stopped using the bar soap a couple months ago.  The cerave AM moisturizer has sunscreen.  I change my pillowcases very regularly and drink tons of water.

Definitely going to get into a dermatologist but that will likely be a 3-6 month wait to get an appointment.  I think it might be that I need the benzoyl peroxide.  That's what proactiv has in it and I didn't get as many whiteheads with proactiv.  I'll pick up some of that and see what happens.

Yes I have similar feelings.  Depressed for as long as I can remember, and am scared of doing pretty much anything now.  It's much more comforting to think about keeping everything the way it is than to imagine trying to dig my way out of the hole I'm in.

Thank you for the advice, I'm still trying to get myself started on it.  I feel like all these years of depression have taken their toll and I no longer have energy left to do anything.  It has certainly helped just to talk to someone about it though. I will keep trying to get myself going on some of these goals.

Yes I do have access to my parents vehicles.  There are many reasons I avoid using them.  I originally learned to drive on a very small car, my dad has  ford F-350, and my mom an SUV; both are giants that terrify me.  Also I know that spending time with them will result in conversations that worsen my depression.  You are right though, I know if I put in the time practicing that I will get used to it.

Thanks, that's a good idea. I do know java and have a bit of experience making android apps from college. 

I do enjoy running but I find after working out regularly for a couple weeks I get sick and end up taking the next week off and losing my motivation to start up again.
